chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha' from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:
I heard him saying: Indeed Allah, the Mighty, the Glorious, hates 'al-qil wa al-qal' (rumor-mongering/gossip), wasting of wealth, and excessive questioning.

key_terms.الْقِيلَ وَالْقَالَ: Rumor-mongering; literally 'the saying and the said', referring to the habit of spreading hearsay and gossip.

ai.seo_question: What are the three things Allah hates according to this hadith from Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) identifies three spiritual corrosives that incur Allah's displeasure: 'al-qil wa al-qal' (gossip and idle talk), 'isadat al-mal' (squandering wealth), and 'kathrat al-su'al' (excessive questioning). This triad highlights the preservation of social harmony, economic prudence, and intellectual focus as key pillars of a righteous life in Shia tradition.
